description: Amid stalled InvestAI deployments and persistent access risks, a subset of EU member states—led by France, Germany, and Poland—initiate a binding regional pact to pool sovereign compute resources for critical infrastructure and emergency response. The agreement includes shared access protocols, joint security audits, and a rotating stewardship model, creating a de facto European AI reserve capacity outside U.S. jurisdiction. This emerges as a bottom-up response to the Union's institutional paralysis and strengthens resilience incrementally.

A widely used open-source software library is found to have been subtly compromised by an AI-generated update that introduces exploitable logic flaws into thousands of downstream applications. The breach evades automated testing and is only detected after unusual system behaviour in critical infrastructure. Attribution points to a non-state actor using open-weight models to design and deploy the attack at scale.
